shortSummary: Fast-bearing myrtle fruit tree renowned for mottled peeling bark, aromatic vitamin-C-packed berries, and tannin-rich medicinal leaves.
leadOverview: Guava (Psidium guajava)—cherished throughout Bengal as Peyara—is one of the most rewarding and nutritionally dense tropical fruit trees on Earth. Native to the Neotropics yet deeply naturalized across Bangladesh's famous floating orchards in Barishal and Pirojpur, its compact crooked canopy bears fragrant white myrtle flowers and crisp, vitamin-C-rich fruits year after year.

sections.title: Morphological Description
sections.subtitle: Coppery mottled flaking bark, four-angled twigs, and pompon stamen blossoms
sections.summary: Detailed breakdown of smooth exfoliating bark, aromatic oil-gland foliage, white brush blossoms, and seedy berries.
paragraphs: Psidium guajava matures into an open, multi-branched small tree 3 to 10 metres tall characterized by smooth, greenish-copper bark that continuously peels away in thin papery flakes to reveal creamy-tan underbark. Young shoots are distinctly four-angled (quadrangular) and softly pubescent, carrying opposite, leathery oblong leaves 7 to 15 centimetres long marked by deeply sunken parallel lateral veins and translucent aromatic oil dots.

Axillary white flowers (2.5–3 cm wide) emerge singly or in pairs from current-season green shoots, crowned by a fluffy tuft of over 200 delicate white stamens tipped with golden anthers. Pollination produces true many-seeded botanical berries—globose to pyriform fruits crowned by a persistent five-lobed calyx, encasing crisp white or fragrant salmon-pink pulp studded with hard kidney-shaped seeds.

subblocks.heading: Exfoliating Copper Bark
subblocks.text: Smooth pale-brown and greenish bark flaking cleanly in thin irregular patches; flexible tough young stems with four ridges.

subblocks.heading: Veined Aromatic Leaves
subblocks.text: Opposite elliptic-oblong leaves featuring 12–18 pairs of deeply impressed lateral veins and fragrant terpene glands.

subblocks.heading: Myrtle Brush Blossoms
subblocks.text: Four or five pure-white petals surrounding a dense pompon of 200–300 creamy stamens rich in pollen and sweet nectar.

subblocks.heading: Crowned Botanical Berries
subblocks.text: Aromatic yellow-green berries topped by a dry calyx ring, enclosing sweet-tart white or lycopene-pink flesh.

sections.title: Taxonomy & Botanical Classification
sections.subtitle: Myrtaceae kinship with Syzygium jam, eucalyptus, and cloves
sections.summary: Taxonomic placement in family Myrtaceae and cultivar diversity across Asia.
paragraphs: Belonging to order Myrtales and family Myrtaceae, Psidium guajava is a close cousin of South Asia's black plum/jamun (Syzygium cumini), rose apple (jamrul), clove (Syzygium aromaticum), and eucalyptus. Across the family, opposite gland-dotted leaves, peeling bark, and brush-like clusters of free stamens serve as reliable morphological hallmarks.
Selective horticultural breeding has yielded world-renowned cultivars tailored for different seasons: Kazi Peyara, BARI Peyara-2, Swarupkathi, Allahabad Safeda, and crisp Thai seedless selections.

sections.title: Natural Habitat & Global Distribution
sections.subtitle: Neotropical origins and Barishal's iconic floating Peyara markets
sections.summary: Global pantropical spread and unique tidal-canal raised-bed cultivation in southern Bangladesh.
paragraphs: Originally domesticated thousands of years ago across southern Mexico, Central America, and northern South America, Spanish and Portuguese galleons carried Psidium guajava across Asia by the seventeenth century. Today it flourishes pan-tropically up to 1,500 metres elevation.

In southern Bangladesh's Swarupkathi (Pirojpur), Jhalokathi, and Barishal delta, growers cultivate vast canal-lined guava gardens on raised earthen beds ('kandi'), transporting mountains of freshly picked green Peyara daily through centuries-old floating boat markets at Bhimruli and Atghar-Kuriana.

sections.title: Ecological Role & Pollinator Interactions
sections.subtitle: Honeybee pollen harvesting, parakeet frugivory, and canopy adaptability
sections.summary: Insect pollination increasing fruit size alongside vertebrate seed dispersal.
paragraphs: While guava flowers can self-pollinate, cross-pollination by honeybees (Apis cerana, Apis mellifera), stingless bees, and syrphid flies drawn to the abundant stamen brushes dramatically increases fruit set and berry weight.

Once berries ripen and release volatile ethyl butyrate aromas, rose-ringed parakeets, fruit bats, and squirrels feast upon the soft pulp, passing hard abrasion-resistant seeds intact across new habitats.

sections.title: Economic, Culinary & Cultural Importance
sections.subtitle: Nutritional vitamin-C powerhouse, pectin jellies, and Bengali Peyara Makha
sections.summary: Unmatched ascorbic acid content, commercial puree processing, and street-food culture.
paragraphs: Gram for gram, fresh guava fruit provides roughly three to four times more vitamin C (over 200 mg per 100 g) than oranges, alongside abundant soluble pectin, potassium, and pink-cultivar lycopene. Across Bangladesh, crisp half-ripe Peyara tossed with mustard oil, green chili, cilantro, and black salt ('Peyara Makha') is a beloved monsoon-to-autumn street snack.
High natural pectin inside guava rinds makes it a premier ingredient for translucent guava jelly, artisanal paste (goiabada), juices, and bakery jams worldwide.

sections.title: Traditional & Scientific Medicinal Properties
sections.subtitle: Quercetin leaf infusions, tannins, and gut-soothing ethnomedicine
sections.summary: Peer-studied antidiarrheal, oral-hygiene, and glycemic-supportive properties of guava leaves.
paragraphs: Guava leaf decoctions are among the most widely validated herbal remedies in tropical ethnomedicine: tender flushed leaves rich in quercetin flavonoids, guaijaverin, ellagic acid, and condensed tannins are brewed across Asia and Latin America to ease acute watery diarrhea and soothe bleeding gums.

Pharmacological trials demonstrate that standardized guava leaf extracts inhibit smooth-muscle intestinal hypermotility, exert broad-spectrum antibacterial activity against enteric pathogens, and mildly blunt post-meal blood-glucose spikes by moderating alpha-glucosidase enzymes.
sections.safetyNote: Frequent large doses of concentrated tannin-rich guava leaf decoctions may worsen constipation or mildly alter oral blood-glucose-lowering medication absorption; monitor blood sugar carefully if combined with antidiabetic drugs.

sections.title: Comprehensive Cultivation & Care Guide
sections.subtitle: Air-layering propagation, crop-regulation pruning, and fruit bagging
sections.summary: Producing sweet winter crops cleanly in pH 5.0–7.5 loam using selective pruning.
paragraphs: Commercial growers propagate elite cultivars via air-layering (guti kolom) or veneer grafting during monsoon, yielding true-to-type fruit within 18 to 24 months. Trees tolerate a broad soil spectrum (pH 5.0–7.5) and even temporary dampness when grown on raised mounds in full sun.

Because guava bears flowers strictly on new vegetative shoots, light post-harvest pruning and withholding water briefly before spring ('bahar' regulation) allow orchardists to shift harvest away from watery monsoon rain into crisp Hemonto–Sheet winter—producing sweeter, less worm-prone fruit especially when young berries are enclosed in breathable white paper bags.

sections.title: Annual Phenology & Six-Season Rhythms
sections.subtitle: Flowering, fruiting, vegetative flush, and Shororitu synchrony
sections.summary: Seasonal cadence across Bengal's six-season cycle (Monsoon (বর্ষা), Late Autumn (হেমন্ত), Winter (শীত)).
paragraphs: Guava (Psidium guajava) aligns its vegetative flushes, anthesis, and fruit maturation tightly with Bengal's Shororitu photoperiod and monsoon moisture transitions, showing peak biological activity during Monsoon (বর্ষা), Late Autumn (হেমন্ত), Winter (শীত).

Monsoon (বর্ষা): Heavy summer-monsoon harvests cascade through southern Bangladesh's floating canal boat markets. Late Autumn (হেমন্ত): Post-monsoon shoot flushes set crisp autumn berries destined for sweet winter ripening. Winter (শীত): Cool dry winter sunlight yields the highest brix sweetness and firmest crunch across Peyara orchards.

sections.title: Seed Germination Biology & Propagation
sections.subtitle: Dormancy regulation, nursery media, and clonal propagation
sections.summary: Reproductive biology and reliable seed or vegetative propagation techniques for Guava.
paragraphs: Guava (Psidium guajava) combines sexual seed propagation—useful for raising sturdy heterozygous rootstocks—with elite clonal techniques such as veneer grafting, air layering (gootee), and semi-hardwood stem cuttings. Fresh recalcitrant or semi-orthodox seeds typically germinate within 14 to 35 days when depulped and sown in warm organic loam.
Clonal orchards standardize crown architecture, early precocity, and uniform biochemical profiles across generations within Myrtaceae.

subblocks.heading: Nursery Seed Protocol
subblocks.text: Depulped seed sown cleanly in 2:1 loam-compost media; high viability when fresh.

subblocks.heading: Clonal Method
subblocks.text: Approach/veneer grafting or monsoon air-layering onto vigorous local rootstocks.

sections.title: Pathology Defense, Vectors & Organic IPM
sections.subtitle: Phytoalexin resilience, fungal prophylaxis, and predator guilds
sections.summary: Biochemical defense mechanisms and low-impact organic IPM guidelines for Psidium guajava.
paragraphs: In humid South Asian and tropical growing belts, Guava (Psidium guajava) relies on secondary terpenoid resins, foliar trichomes, and phytoalexin phenolics as front-line biochemical deterrence against herbivores and opportunistic pathogens. Prolonged monsoon waterlogging or stagnant canopy humidity can nonetheless encourage anthracnose (Colletotrichum spp.), powdery mildew, leaf-spot fungi, or root-zone Pythium.

Organic Integrated Pest Management (IPM) prioritizes preventive airflow pruning, Trichoderma-enriched compost amendments around feeder roots, and targeted cold-pressed Azadirachta indica (neem) oil sprays at dusk to suppress sap-sucking aphids, scale insects, and mealybugs without harming native pollinators.

subblocks.heading: Fungal Management
subblocks.text: Prevent overhead foliar wetness at dusk; maintain canopy aeration and copper/Trichoderma prophylaxis.

subblocks.heading: Organic Pest Control
subblocks.text: Neem kernel emulsion (3–5 ml/L) plus conservation of hoverfly and ladybird predator guilds.

sections.title: Conservation Standing & Climate Resilience
sections.subtitle: Population security, agroforestry corridors, and stress tolerance
sections.summary: Biogeographic conservation standing and climate adaptation traits of Guava.
paragraphs: Across its native and naturalized distribution (Tropical Americas (Mexico to Northern South America)), Guava (Psidium guajava) demonstrates strong ecological plasticity across alluvial floodplains, homestead agroforestry plots, and urban biodiversity corridors. While cultivated stands remain broadly secure, landrace genetic erosion, coastal salinity shifts, and wetland drainage threaten wild ecotypes and heritage regional varieties.

Long-term resilience depends on decentralized in-situ homestead stewardship, wetland buffer conservation, and botanical garden germplasm collections preserving drought-, flood-, and salinity-tolerant alleles amid shifting monsoon regimes.

subblocks.heading: Ecological Resilience
subblocks.text: Adapted to Tropical Americas (Mexico to Northern South America) thermal oscillations and seasonal hydrological extremes.

subblocks.heading: Stewardship Strategy
subblocks.text: Preserve traditional landraces, pollinator corridors, and living herbarium voucher plots.

sections.title: Horticultural Spacing, Pruning & Telemetry
sections.subtitle: Plot geometry, canopy shaping, and calibrated soil-climate meters
sections.summary: Calibrated horticultural parameters: pH 5.0 – 7.5, Full Sun (6–8 hrs), and structural spacing guidance.
paragraphs: Optimal managed cultivation of Guava (Psidium guajava) calibrates root-zone chemistry around pH 5.0 – 7.5 inside fertile well-drained loam. Providing adequate crown spacing prevents humidity buildup and lets lower shoots capture uniform irradiance across full sun (6–8 hrs).

Light corrective pruning immediately after main flowering or harvest periods redirects assimilates into healthy vegetative framework, while moisture scheduling (moderate / pruning-guided) stabilizes root turgor without inducing hypoxia.

sections.title: Evolutionary Genetics & Adaptive Phylogeny
sections.subtitle: Myrtales clade divergence and Myrtaceae genomic traits
sections.summary: Phylogenetic placement of genus Psidium within order Myrtales (Eudicot (Malvids)).
paragraphs: Modern molecular phylogenetics (APG IV) places Psidium guajava inside family Myrtaceae (মিরটাসি (জাম-পেয়ারা গোত্র)), order Myrtales, clade Eudicot (Malvids). Aromatic myrtle trees and shrubs distinguished by peeling mottled bark, opposite oil-gland foliage, and powder-puff blossoms bristling with hundreds of stamens.

Within genus Psidium, specialized morphological adaptations—such as exfoliating smooth copper-brown bark flaking in papery patches—reflect co-evolutionary specialization with regional pollinator guilds and abiotic habitat filters.

sections.title: Field Identification Key & Diagnostic Checks
sections.subtitle: Macro-morphological verification against look-alike taxa
sections.summary: Rapid field-sheet checklist for confirming Psidium guajava (Peyara (পেয়ারা)).
paragraphs: Field verification of Guava (Psidium guajava) rests on recognizing key Myrtaceae family markers: Exfoliating smooth copper-brown bark flaking in papery patches; Opposite leathery leaves dotted with fragrant terpenoid oil glands; Showy stamen-tufted blossoms yielding aromatic crowned berries and drupes. Inspecting fresh leaf arrangement, stem surface texture, and reproductive architecture together eliminates confusion with sympatric congeners.

Exfoliating Copper Bark: Smooth pale-brown and greenish bark flaking cleanly in thin irregular patches; flexible tough young stems with four ridges. Veined Aromatic Leaves: Opposite elliptic-oblong leaves featuring 12–18 pairs of deeply impressed lateral veins and fragrant terpene glands. Myrtle Brush Blossoms: Four or five pure-white petals surrounding a dense pompon of 200–300 creamy stamens rich in pollen and sweet nectar. Crowned Botanical Berries: Aromatic yellow-green berries topped by a dry calyx ring, enclosing sweet-tart white or lycopene-pink flesh.
